purpose: Test whether a mechanically compiled change contract reduces a coding agent's repository-exploration cost without degrading independently verified correctness.
northStarQuestion: Can Rapture remove enough repeated repository-discovery work from a coding agent to measurably improve verified engineering efficiency?

baseline.whyStacked: The hypothesis is that precomputed context removes repository-discovery work. Main's only corpus (real-work-v0) has 7-8 file fixtures of ~2.6KB with a 16-line maximum source file, which an agent reads in two tool calls; there is no discovery cost there for a contract to remove, so measuring on it would return a null result by construction. The delegation-v0 corpus on PR #9 has 52-file and 127KB repositories with 1416- and 2790-line source files, and carries measured per-task acceptance needed for the pre-registered task selection. That functionality is genuinely required, so this branch stacks and both PRs must land in order.

conditions.description: OpenCode receives the task specification and normal repository access only.
Identical in every respect, plus .rapture/change-contract.json present in the worktree and a fixed sentence pointing at it.

design.onlyVariable: presence of the compiled change contract in the worktree, and the fixed pointer sentence naming it
design.pairingNote: Both conditions live in the same task file so they interleave within a trial, pairing them in time rather than running all of one condition first.

configuration.executionStructure: Three runner invocations, one per repository, because a run materializes worktrees from a single base revision. Each invocation carries that repository's selected tasks in both conditions.

taskSelection.rule: Chosen before execution using acceptance measured in the delegation workstream. Four tasks sit away from the ceiling so acceptance can move in either direction; four are at ceiling, which is where exploration cost can be read without acceptance noise. Task set is fixed and will not be changed after seeing results.
taskSelection.hardNegativeControlNote: version-diff-release-type has never been accepted in 9 prior attempts. If the contract condition were to 'solve' it, that would indicate leakage rather than assistance and must be investigated before any positive claim.

requirements: Acceptance in the contract condition is not more than 5 percentage points below baseline.
At least two exploration-cost metrics improve by >= 20% in median paired comparison.
Improvement direction is consistent in at least two of three repetitions for a majority of tasks.
The result is not explained by one pathological task.
No material increase in scope violations or infrastructure/provider failures.

conditions: No material reduction in exploration cost.
Or the apparent improvement is dominated by one task or confounded by different validation behaviour.
Variance too high to read a direction.
Corpus too easy or too hard to discriminate the conditions.

successCriteria.rule: These thresholds are fixed before execution and will not be adjusted after seeing results.

instrumentation.source: OpenCode structured JSON event stream (tool_use events)
instrumentation.nullPolicy: Any metric the stream does not support is null. Host telemetry is not used as a substitute because it cannot attribute work to an agent action.

contractDelivery.mechanism: .rapture/change-contract.json written into the worktree before the agent starts, with .rapture/ added to the worktree git exclude file so it is readable but never appears as a change the agent made
contractDelivery.promptDelta: One fixed sentence naming the file and stating it contains no solution. The engineering request itself is byte-identical across conditions.

preflight.knownGoodLeakCheck: 0 leaks across 760 solution lines x 8 contracts

prohibitedConclusions: That the Agentic Change Compiler vision is validated, unless exploration improves materially without degrading acceptance.
Any causal mechanism beyond the paired intervention actually tested.
Generalization to other repositories, models, agents or hosts.
That routing, swarms, scheduling or further compiler layers are justified.
